data.name: Ashmika
data.gender_notes: Ashmika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ashmika is a Sanskrit name derived from the Ashmaka tree, which is believed to symbolize life and longevity. The name is often associated with the goddess Ashmakini, who is known for her nurturing and protective qualities. In Hindu mythology, Ashmika is believed to bring happiness, prosperity, and good fortune. The name Ashmika carries the meaning “Nectar of life” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashmika usually hope their child will grow to embody nectar of life and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ashmika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nectar of life.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashmika total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Ashmika was a celebrated poetess and musician in ancient India, renowned for her exquisite compositions in Sanskrit and Telugu languages. She is believed to have lived during the 6th and 7th centuries CE in the southern Indian region of Andhra Pradesh, and is considered an important figure in the Bhakti movement which emphasized devotion to deities through music and literature.

Another reference suggests that Ashmika was a queen of the Vakataka dynasty in the Deccan region of India around the 5th century CE. She is known for her contributions to the construction of numerous temples and her patronage of scholars and artists during her reign.
